Execute an Rmd (Rmarkdown) script from shell

Source: R/execute_from_shell.R
Rmdbatch.Rd

Rmdbatch() essentially creates a temporary R script executing rmarkdown::render(file, ...), which is then executed with Rbatch(). It is assumed that your Rmarkdown script creates html output.

Rmdbatch(
  file,
  destdir = ".",
  outfile = paste0(basename(file), ".Rout"),
  timing = TRUE,
  destdir.html = dirname(file),
  outfile.html = sub("Rmd$", "html", file),
  overwrite.html = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

file

Path and name of an Rmarkdown script to be executed. Must have extension .Rmd.

destdir

Output directory for .Rout-file (R console).

outfile

Name of output .Rout file (R console), NOT including folder name - use destdir for that!

timing

Logical: print execution time in console?

destdir.html

Where to move the html output file (assuming knitr is generating html output)

outfile.html

Name of the output html file, NOT including folder name - use destdir.html for that!

overwrite.html

Logical: Whether to overwrite an existing html file in folder destdir.html.

...

Passed to rmarkdown::render().

Value

Character string: path to the output log file.

Details

Rmdbatch produces two output files: A log file (contents that would be written to the R console) and a html report:

  • To specify the log file, use the parameters destdir (default: current working directory) and outfile (default: name of input file with .Rout appended).

  • To specify the html file, use the parameters destdir.html (default: directory of input file) and outfile.html (default: name of input file, but with extension .html instead of .Rmd).
